result.title: Local Evidence, Global Failure: Diagnosing Speech-Vision Temporal Composition in Audio-Visual Language Models
result.summary: Audio-visual large language models (AV-LLMs) can fail at full-video speech-vision decisions even when useful visual evidence is locally recoverable. We introduce Temporal Evidence Decomposition (TED), a training-free diagnostic framework that separates local visual verification from speech-relative aggregation. Automatic speech recognition supplies a transcript and utterance interval. TED queries audio-free windows with the transcript for Temporal Alignment and Forecasting, or answer candidates for Cross-Modal Temporal Binding, then aggregates evidence relative to that interval. Across four frozen AV-LLMs on SVHalluc, Temporal Forecasting accuracy rises from 29.3-33.7% under full-video questioning to 79.3-82.2% with TED. Query replacement reduces recovery; the observed anchor remains beneficial when temporal-region availability is held fixed. Physical-isolation and timing-shortcut controls test alternative explanations. The findings distinguish locally recoverable evidence from successful full-video decisions, motivating explicit separation of narration content, utterance timing, and time-indexed visual evidence.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出免训练的 Temporal Evidence Decomposition（TED）诊断框架，把音频-视觉大模型的「局部视觉验证」与「相对语音的聚合」拆开：由 ASR 给出转录与话语区间，在无音频窗口上用转录做时间对齐与预测、或用候选答案做跨模态时间绑定，再按该区间聚合证据，用于诊断全视频语音-视觉决策的失败。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及多模态推理中「局部可恢复证据」与「全视频决策失败」的落差，与视觉证据筛选、证据获取与聚合、时间对齐等兴趣点相关，可供核查其证据分离诊断能否迁移到 LVR 的 latent 状态与证据使用评估。
